ds_value: Monitor equipment operation and condition for aft end compressor rubs
Integrate inspection for aft end compressor rubs with yearly scheduled borescope inspection per GER 3620
Observe rotor blade stages 13 through 17 and look for mushroomed material, bluing at the blade tip, and/or markings in the casing area
If rubs or tip loss occur, blending to increase clearances can be performed at Major Inspections (MI) or when the Compressor Discharge Casing (CDC) is removed
During repairs, clearances of rotor blades can be increased radially by tip grinding and polishing, and tip corners repaired by blade blending (typically 20 mils radially)
Following tip grinding/polishing, a penetrant inspection must be performed to ensure no tip cracks are present
our_value: Borescope inspection of rotor blade stages 13 through 17
Blade blending and tip grinding/polishing if rubs or tip loss are found
Penetrant inspection of blade tips after grinding/polishing
Clearance measurement and adjustment

ds_value: Follow operating practices per GER 3620 to reduce the potential for rubs on aft end compressor blades
Keep enclosure doors closed during startup, shutdown and normal operation

Be aware that restarting the gas turbine between 2 and 8 hours following a shutdown or trip will cause clearances in the aft end to decrease; include this area in yearly borescope inspections if unit operates this way
Eliminate any potential pipe leaks that may cause quenching of the gas turbine compressor discharge casing
Ensure vent fans and exhaust fans to the gas turbine enclosure are functioning properly such that no local forced convection is taking place at or near the compressor discharge casing
Integrate the inspection for aft end compressor rubs with yearly scheduled borescope inspection per GER 3620; observe rotor blade stages 13 through 17
If rubs or tip loss occur, perform blending at Major Inspection or when CDC is removed; typically remove 20 mils radially to increase clearance and remove heat affected and rolled over material
Following tip grinding/polishing operation, perform penetrant inspection to ensure no tip cracks are present
our_value: Keep enclosure doors closed during startup, shutdown and normal operation.
Eliminate any potential pipe leaks that may cause quenching of the gas turbine compressor discharge casing.
Ensure vent fans and exhaust fans to the gas turbine enclosure are functioning properly such that no local forced convection is taking place at or near the compressor discharge casing.
Integrate the inspection for aft end compressor rubs with your yearly scheduled borescope inspection per GER 3620.
Observe rotor blade stages 13 through 17 and look for mushroomed material, bluing at the blade tip, and / or markings in the casing area.
If rubs or tip loss do occur, perform blending to increase clearances at Major Inspections (MI) or when the Compressor Discharge Casing (CDC) is removed.
Increase clearances of rotor blades radially by tip grinding and polishing (typically 20 mils) and repair tip corners by blade blending.
Perform a penetrant inspection after grinding/polishing to ensure no tip cracks are present.

ds_value: Remove turbine blades prior to beginning inspections per hot gas path outage scope
CO2 blast cleaning of turbine rotor (one shift / 12 hours), including prior hand wiping to remove oil from dovetail surfaces if necessary
ECI of first and second stages (three shifts), or all three stages in four shifts
Total time between turbine blade removal and installation should be four shifts (two days) - estimates only
Visual inspection of all exposed turbine rotor surfaces
Borescope inspection of accessible rotor surfaces
FPI of staked balance weight grooves and lock wire tab fillets
UT of counterbore outside diameter ligaments on distance piece and turbine aft shaft
our_value: Remove turbine blades prior to beginning inspections.
Clean turbine rotor using dry ice (CO2) blasting (preferred method, 12 hours).
Perform Eddy Current Inspection (ECI) of Stage 1 and 2 turbine wheel dovetails (approx. 32 hours).
Perform Visual and Borescope (BI) inspection of all exposed turbine rotor surfaces.
Perform Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI) on balance weights and lockwire tabs.
Perform Ultrasonic (UT) inspection of counterbore outside diameter ligaments on distance piece and turbine aft shaft.
Install dovetail modified (back cut) Stage 1 and 2 turbine blades.

ds_value: Perform ECI, Visual, BI, FPI, and UT every 24 khrs or 900 starts for wheels fired without shot peening (original cooling slot, original balance rail/LWT)
Perform ECI every 48 khrs or 2,400 starts for 2 Step Age wheels with original cooling slot that were never fired without shot peening (every 24 khrs or 900 starts if back cut buckets not installed)
Perform ECI at 96 khrs or 3,600 starts for 2 Step Age Stage 1 wheels with contoured or enhanced cooling slot (every 48 khrs or 2,400 starts if back cut buckets not installed for contoured)
Perform ECI at 96 khrs or 3,600 starts for 2 Step Age Stage 1 enhanced wheels with stakeless & modified tab
For Stage 2 wheels with 2 Step Age: ECI at 96 khrs or 3,750 starts if specific S2B P/N installed (inspection window 80-104 khrs), otherwise at first Major after TW2 Life Extension
Perform BI every HGPI when CDC is not removed for applicable Stage 1 wheels
Perform FPI on LWT every HGPI when buckets are removed; on BWG every Major and when CDC is removed during HGPI
For stakeless & modified tab wheels: FPI LWT every Major only
For 3 Step Age wheels: FPI LWT every Major only
Install back cut (modified) turbine blades on all turbine rotors at next scheduled maintenance
TW3 staked BWG: FPI every MI and when Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI; stakeless: no inspections necessary
TW3 original LWT: FPI every HGPI while buckets are removed; modified LWT: FPI every MI
TAS staked BWG: FPI every MI and when Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI; stakeless: no inspections necessary
Contact GE Vernova representative for peening modification wheels to determine applicable peening condition based on turbine serial number
If cooling slot crack is detected, immediate wheel replacement is recommended to avoid risk of wheel post liberation during operation
If crack-like indications found on LWT or BWG, contact GE Vernova for disposition; in-situ repair procedure may be used
our_value: Perform ECI on Stage 1 and 2 turbine wheel dovetails at intervals specified by configuration (Material Heat Treatment, Peening, Cooling Slot Geometry).
Perform Visual/BI inspection of broach slot fillets, slot bottoms, tangs, cooling slots, spacer rim seal tooth rubs, and balance weights.
Perform FPI on staked balance weight grooves at every Major inspection and when CDC is removed during HGPI.
Perform FPI on lock wire tab fillets when turbine blades are removed.
Perform UT on counterbore outside diameter ligaments on distance piece and turbine aft shaft.
Install dovetail modified (back cut) Stage 1 and 2 turbine blades at the next scheduled maintenance (HGPI or Major).
Perform FPI on Stage 3 wheel and turbine aft shaft staked balance weight grooves every Major and when Exhaust Frame is removed during HGPI.
Perform FPI on Stage 3 wheel lockwire tabs (Original: every HGPI; Modified: every Major).
